acts.lead:
Read the selection below and answer the questions that follow.

HOW A DOG’S LIFE WAS SAVED

Bernie, a police dog, loves Boy
Scouts and he really has a very good
reason for doing so. He would have died
were it not for the training of two Boy
Scouts who knew how to make a
tourniquet. These two boys who were twins
were members of the Narra Troop Number
64.

The two boys were on their way home from school. They were busy
talking about the Boy Scout Jamboree to be held in Japan. They were lucky
to be among the Boy Scouts to represent the Philippines in the jamboree.

“Look!” cried Nick, one of the twins. “See the blood trail on the
sidewalk.”

Because Boy Scouts are trained to be of help in time of trouble, they
followed the trail. It led them to the backyard of a certain Mr. Gana. They
heard a feeble whine. Behind the pile of boxes they found Mr. Gana’s dog, Bernie.
He seemed very weak due to loss of blood and looked completely exhausted as
he lay.

Bernie greeted the two boys with a feeble wag of his tail. The two boys
had hopes of saving his life. If only they could stop the bleeding of his wounded
foot.

“I will get my handkerchief,” said Pete reaching into his pocket. “Do you
have something to bind it with, Nick?”

The boys did not waste any time. Nick pulled a lead pencil out of his
pocket. Pete tore a strip about two or three inches wide from the handkerchief.
He folded it over and over three or four times making a strong narrow band.
Pete tied the two ends together while Nick held Bernie. Then Pete skipped the
band over the dog’s injured foot. Bernie bore the pain without wincing as the
two boys tightened the tourniquet.

When the bleeding stopped, the boys went to Mr. Gana and told him
what had happened to Bernie. Mr. Gana returned home as soon as possible
and found Bernie’s wound well taken care of.

The boys then tried to find out how it all happened. They followed the
trail back to where Bernie met the accident. Apparently, Bernie had
accidentally stepped on a broken bottle.

Bernie would have bled to death had it not been for the two boys and
their tourniquet. This is why Bernie has an excellent reason for loving the Boy
Scouts. He never fails to lick Pete’s and Nick’s hands whenever they pass by
their home. The twins had a special place in Bernie’s heart.

Read each question thoroughly. Choose the letter of the correct answer.

Literal Reading Skill
These questions focus on facts explicitly stated in the text.

items.text: Where was the Boy Scout Jamboree that Nick and Pete were selected to attend?
What two specific items did the twins use to stop Bernie’s bleeding?
opts: A handkerchief and a lead pencil
A piece of string and a ruler
A shoelace and a pen These questions require you to "read between the lines" and draw inferences.

items.text: Why did the boys choose to follow the blood trail instead of going straight home?
opts: They were curious to see if there was a crime
They wanted to find a lost pet for a reward
Their training taught them to provide help during trouble
They were looking for a broken bottle

items.text: What does the "feeble wag" of Bernie’s tail suggest about his condition when the boys found him?
opts: He was energetic and ready to play
He was extremely weak but still friendly or hopeful
He was angry that the boys entered the yard
He was trying to lead them to the broken bottle These questions involve evaluating the text, the characters' decisions, and the author’s purpose.

items.text: How would you evaluate the twins’ decision to use a lead pencil in their medical intervention?
opts: It was a mistake because pencils are too fragile for medical use
It was unnecessary because the bleeding would have stopped on its own
It was a resourceful use of available tools to create a functional tourniquet
It was a lucky guess that didn't actually help stop the blood

items.text: What is the author’s primary purpose in mentioning that Bernie is a "police dog"?
opts: To explain why Bernie was so aggressive toward the twins
To show that the Boy Scouts were breaking the law
To highlight the irony that a dog trained to help others needed to be helped himself
To suggest that Bernie was injured while catching a criminal

items.text: Which statement best analyzes the reliability of the boys' scout training as presented in the story?
opts: The training was outdated because they didn't have a real medical kit
The training was highly effective as it provided life-saving skills for emergency situations
The training was only useful because the boys were twins
The training was focused more on travel than on first aid These questions ask you to think beyond the text and apply the information to new scenarios.

items.text: If Nick and Pete had not found a pencil in their pockets, which of these items from a student's bag would be the best substitute to tighten the tourniquet?
opts: A single sheet of notebook paper
A small piece of scotch tape

items.text: Based on the ending of the story, what is the most likely way Bernie would react if he saw Nick and Pete in a large crowd of people?
opts: He would likely seek them out specifically to show affection
He would ignore them because there are too many people
He would bark at them to warn them of more broken glass
He would hide because he associates them with the pain of the tourniquet

items.text: Imagine the "Narra Troop 64" wanted to create a commemorative badge for the twins. What symbol would most accurately represent this specific rescue?
opts: A picture of a school building
A handkerchief tied around a pencil
A broken bottle on a sidewalk

THE MOST DESTRUCTIVE CREATURES
ON EARTH
Rats are probably the cleverest
and the most destructive animals on
earth. These animals can survive
anywhere. They have also threatened
man's life; rat-borne diseases have
killed more people than all the wars in
history.

Most of the 650 species of rats live
in forests, fields, and jungles. But a species tries to link their destinies with men.
They go where men go, live where they live, eat what they eat, and learn their
ways.

There are two species of common house rats - the brown rat and the
black rat. The brown rat has small ears and thick tail that is shorter than its
body. It may weigh as much as one-half kilogram and measure nine inches in
length, minus its tail. The brown rat is a burrower. It can squeeze through
the sewers for miles and enter a man's home through the plumbing.

The black rat is very much smaller than the brown rat. It has an average
weight of one-fourth kilogram. It has large eyes and a tail longer than its body.
The black rat, clambers up walls, ropes, and wires.

Rats are social animals and live in colonies. They wage wars against
others and an "outsider" is killed by torture known only to rats.

The average life of a rat is nine months, although some may live up to
two years. They are very prolific. It has been estimated that a pair of rats, if
allowed to multiply unmolested, could produce up to 350 million descendants
in three years.

Everywhere the rats go, they spread contamination. which is a
continuing health menace. They carry as many as 35 different diseases. Their
fleas spread bubonic plague and typhus. These two diseases have killed more
than 200 million people in for countries.

The rat's habits take them from sewer to warehouse to home, spreading
disease germs every step of the way. They leave droppings everywhere they go
and contaminate everything because in their blood and intestines are
organisms that cause dysentery, tularemia, rabies, and many other
contagious killer diseases.
Nature has endowed rats with special characteristics to help them
survive. They avoid poison but after one or two members had felt its effects.
They leave their urine on everything that poison-tainted as a "keep-off" sign
to other
rats.

But there is one way rats become useful to man; Man makes use of rats
in his studies of drugs, medicine, and the treatment of disease.

Read the selection below and answer the questions that follow.

COCONUT, THE TREE OF LIFE
The coconut is a tropical
palm. It provides man with
almost     everything;   food,
clothing,     shelter,  home
furnishings, fuel, and many
others. On the products of the
coconut tree, one can subsist
almost fully.

The coconut grows palm
leaf every month. Each leaf bears a cluster of flowers which mature into
clusters of fruits. High at the top of the crown of leaves is the coconut heart
or bud. If the heart or the bud is removed, the tree dies. The heart itself makes
a tasty treat, a "millionaire's salad."

The unopened flowers are protected by a tough sheath that looks like
burlap. From this sheath may be fashioned our shoes, caps, and even a kind
of helmet.

Sugar may be obtained from the sap of the unopened flowers. A gallon
of sap may be gathered and boiled to a good syrup which can be crystallized
into rich, dark sugar. Or if left standing, the sap ferments quickly into a robust
beer-like drink called "tuba" in the Philippines, "toddy" in India, "tuwak" in
Indonesia. If left alone for a few weeks; the sap becomes fine vinegar.

The nut itself is covered by a thick, packed mass of fibers called "coir"
which can be woven into strong twine or rope. Coir is also used in padding
upholstery. The shell of the coconut is hard, fine-grained substance which
can be carved into all kinds of objects; cups, ashtrays, button, buckles, and
many others. The charcoal from shells is used as air filters in gas masks,
submarines, and cigarette tips.

Coconut water contains sugar, minerals, and vitamins, The nut meat is
eaten raw or made into salad; coconut milk is used in cooking food. Heated,
it yields oil for cooking, lamp fuel, lotions, pomades, and soaps.

Grated nut meats are made into candies, cakes, and pies. Dried coconut
meat or "copra" is processed for oil and the residue is made into animal food.

There are many uses of the coconut oil. It is used in shampoos, soaps,
toothpaste, lotion, lubricants, hydraulic fluid, paints, synthetic rubber, ice
cream, plastics, and others. It is also found in breakfast tables - "margarine"
as a substitute for butter with all the needed nutrients and vitamins.

There are plenty of uses for the rest of the tree. The fronds are woven
into mats and house furnishings, the midribs made into brooms and brushes.
Even the roots can be made into dyes.

No other tree on earth is as useful and as the coconut!

Read each question thoroughly. Choose the letter of the correct answer.

opts: A thick, packed mass of fibers covering the nut.

PRISON WITHOUT WALLS
In 1904, the Iwahig Penal
Colony was built. It was a kind of
prison where- in long term
prisoners, most of them life. The
colony was originally, designed to
house an overflow of termers,
serve    their  sentences     with
comparative freedom. convicts
from Manila's old Bilibid Prison.
Its basic purpose was to reform
and rehabilitate criminals rather than punish them. It is under the
supervision of the superintendent of prisons.

The settlement site was once a 34- square mile of virgin jungle. The first
prisoners hacked out roads, prepared the fields and slanted coconuts and
other fruit-bearing trees. Through the years, the colony has expanded to cover
160square miles of cultivated land.

Only prisoners with comparatively long sentences are assigned at the
Iwahig Penal Colony. Newly arrived inmates are quartered in disciplinary
barracks for at least six months. They do not have the same privileges as the
old-time colonial. Later, when they are fully indoctrinated with the rules and
regulations of the colony as well as their duties and obligations, they are
assigned to various projects where they can put their special skills to good
use.

Illiterate inmates attend adult education classes handled by teachers
who are fellow convicts. The children of inmates are educated in schools and
reading centers in the settlement. Medical treatment is available at the
prison's hospital.

The inmates sleep in spacious barrack-rooms with no barred windows
to prevent them from breaking out. They are free to marry, but must have
permission of the Director of Prisons to do so. If married, arrangements could
be made from their families to live in the settlement. They are free to go about
within the 160-square mile limits of the penal colony.

Like their free compatriots, the inmates work for a living from P500 to
P1,000 a month by farming, fishing, forestry, animal husbandry,

construction, jobs in the coconut and coffee industries, and handicrafts. The
colony's extensive forests provide them with wood which they can sell. They
can fish in the coastal waters or raise poultry and meat animals for their
consumption. But as inmates, they have to work for the prison industries,
too, for certain hours and days of the week.

The atmosphere in the colony is quiet good such that some convicts
prefer to stay there permanently even when their sentences expired. Deserving
Ex-convicts who choose to stay in the colony permanently are granted small
plots of land for their use. Thus, social derelicts are turned useful citizens.

A MOTHER'S WISDOM
Barbara was 10 when she was
found her first real "pal" among the
girls in school. Their friendship
became all-important to Barbara,
and being of a possessive nature,
she found herself violently jealous
of her friend's interests which did
not include Barbara. She couldn't
conceal this attitude until her friend
became annoyed with her possessiveness.

Barbara's mother understood what was happening. She waited for an
occasion to talk to Barbara about it without hurting her.

One day, Barbara and her mother were admiring some baby chicks.
Barbara picked up one and held it so tightly that it almost smothered. It
struggled to escape from Barbara's hold. Casually her mother said, "If you
hold a chick too tightly, it wants only to get away. Try holding one gently."

The next chick nestled quietly in Barbara's open palm. Her mother said,
"You know, dear, people are the same as chicks. If we hold those whom we
love too closely to us, they'll struggle for freedom. Hold them with open hands
and they won't feel smothered."

Barbara understood the message in her mother's words. Whenever she
felt jealous of her friend's attention to others, she always pictures the
contented chick nestled in her open palm.

Joseph, Barbara's brother was eight. Being young and mischievous, he
used to get into jams and then run to his mother for help to get him out of
trouble. But Mother never interfered. She would let him untangle his troubles
by himself. Joseph never understood why Mother always declined to help him
with his problems.

One day, Joseph saw a cocoon of a moth throbbing and heaving.
Squealing with anticipation, Joseph began to open the cocoon with his pocket
knife to allow the moth to emerge more easily. To his disappointment, the

moth did not fly; it fell off from the twig on which the cocoon hung, then died
that very same moment.

Joseph's mother shook him on the shoulders and said, "Son, the
struggle of the moth inside the cocoon was for a purpose, to enable it to gain
strength to rise above its surroundings. You did not allow it to mature fully,
and when you forcibly opened the cocoon, it can neither walk nor fly. It's the
same with children. When a boy like you always has somebody to solve his
problems for him, he has no chance to develop, Each of the struggles that we
go through on our own builds up our strength to meet the next."

Barbara and Joseph never forget the lessons they learned from their
mother.

Barbara should stop being friends with people who make her feel jealous.

opts: The physical pain someone feels when they get into trouble.
The difficult challenges people face that help them grow stronger and more independent.
The time a person spends waiting for someone else to help them solve a problem.
The act of hiding away from the world when things get too hard.

opts: She was too busy watching the baby chicks with Barbara.
She wanted to punish him for being mischievous and getting into "jams".
She knew that solving his problems for him would prevent him from developing his own strength.
She did not believe that an eight-year-old was old enough to have real problems.

opts: The moth died because it missed the necessary process of gaining strength through its own efforts.
The moth died because Joseph used a pocket knife that was too sharp.
The moth died because it was not mature enough to see the sunlight.
The moth died because it fell off the twig before it could learn how to walk.

opts: It made them fear their mother because she wouldn't help them.
It provided them with mental "pictures" and lessons that helped them handle their own emotions and problems.
It encouraged them to spend more time outside with nature instead of going to school.
It taught them that they should never ask for help, even in an emergency.

LIGHTNING AND THUNDER
Lightning is the same thing as
light in an electric bulb. It is
electricity. A flash of lightning has
twenty times as much electricity as
the world uses in 24 hours.

Electricity is always present in the
air. When moisture in the air
condenses on a tiny grain of dust, the
little drop becomes charged with
electricity. Then, when the air gets cold and the drops go together to make
raindrops, some of the electricity cannot stay on the drops and has to get off.
When millions of drops of water are pushing off little bits of electricity, they
all go together and make one big flash of lightning.

Flashes of lightning usually go from one cloud to another, they
sometimes hit the ground. Lightning is hot. When it hits a house, the later
gets burned. When it strikes a tree, the heat turns the tree's sap into steam
which must escape quickly, and thus the tree splits open. It may hit a wire
fence and lightning travels along the wire just as electricity travels along a
write to a lamp.

To protect tall buildings from lightning, lightning rods are put into the
ground at the side of the building. People used to think that the rod attracts
the lightning and when it strikes the rod, the rod carries the lightning through
the wire into the ground. Actually, the rod helps to make the lightning strike
somewhere else. The rod allows the ground electricity to come up slowly
through the rod and into the air. Lightning does not strike in a place where
other electricity comes out slowly.

The safest place during a thunderstorm is in the house. Open windows
do not attract lightning as people used to think.

Out of doors, it is not safe to stay under a tree for trees are often struck
by lightning. In open fields, the safest thing to do during a thunderstorm is to
lie flat on the ground.

Lightning does not make any sound. It makes a big flash like a million
lamps put together. Along the flash comes a long roll of noise which we call

thunder. It is sometimes so far off that it is just faint mutter; at other times it
is so close overhead that it sounds like cannons firing.

Thunder sometimes frighten people although it cannot do any harm.
When lightning strikes, air becomes heated so quickly that it explodes into
thunder.

Lightning and thunder seldom do any damage. There is no reason for
people to be afraid of them.

To warn people that lightning rods are dangerous because they attract lightning.

To explain that lightning is made of glass and wire.
To use a familiar object to help the reader visualize the incredible brightness and power of a flash.
To argue that people should turn off their lamps during a thunderstorm.

THE GREAT CHINESE TEACHER
Confucius' teachings had left an indelible mark in
the lives of millions of Chinese.

Thousands of years ago in a flowery kingdom in
the state of Lu lived a soldier Known as Kung, the
Tall. He was so-called because he was seven feet tall.
When he reached his seventieth birthday he reflected
sorrowfully over his life. He had nine children and all
of them were girls. He had no son to carry on his
family name and to perform the rites and ceremonies
of ancestors worship. This was practiced by the
Chinese throughout the centuries to show their
reverence to their forefathers. Kung, the Tall came from a noble lineage and
he would not want to break this tradition.

Two years before his death, a son was born to him. His son, named
Confucius, became known as a "Great Sage" and philosopher to China and
the world beyond China. His words and wisdom have such a vast influence
on the thoughts and on the ways of life of the Chinese throughout five
centuries. He was called Master King.

The Chinese already lived in beautiful houses with fine furniture, grew
crops, used agricultural implements and spun silk for their clothing. They
used coins, marked time by the moon and had developed cooking to a fine
taste. They already had law courts and schools where history, music and
literature were taught. They wrote books by hand on bamboo and they bound
the pages together with thongs.

Master Kung was a scholar in school. He had two special interests: first,
how people should live and conduct themselves; and second, how the state
should be governed. When he grew up to manhood he traveled all over the
civilized world with a band of disciples. Two or three times, he was given
positions of importance in the government but he never stayed long in these
positions. The officers in the government resented Master Kung's honesty.
Confucius continued teaching not knowing that his ideas were to be passed
on from generation to generation, that thousands of books were to be written
about him and his sayings, that he was to become one of the most beloved
and revered men in history.

He preached the importance the importance of courtesy, orderliness,
loyalty, justice, and devotion to one's parents. He emphasized that the
government should be governed by men who possessed these virtues. He
stressed the importance of happiness in family life and of endurance and
consideration for one's neighbors.

These beautiful thoughts had become part of the national character of
the Chinese people. They were taught that happiness can be found in
cultivating the art of living and in calm and settled existence.

Confucius' greatest influence in Chinese life was family reverence and
bonds of family life. He always believed that reverence for one's ancestors was
important and desirable.

They did not believe that a teacher should be allowed to hold a position of importance.
His honest nature and high moral standards likely exposed or interfered with their own less-virtuous ways of governing.
They felt that his focus on music and literature was a waste of the government's time.

opts: "They wrote books by hand on bamboo and they bound the pages together with thongs."
"Two or three times, he was given positions of importance in the government."
"Happiness can be found in cultivating the art of living and in calm and settled existence."
"He had nine children and all of them were girls."

opts: To show that Kung, the Tall was a very successful and wealthy man.

To suggest that Confucius had a difficult childhood growing up with nine sisters.
To prove that soldiers in ancient China were required to have large families.

items.text: What is the author’s primary purpose in mentioning that the Chinese already lived in beautiful houses and used coins before Confucius began teaching?
opts: To establish that Confucius lived in a highly developed and civilized society, making his intellectual influence even more impressive.

To explain why Confucius decided to travel the world instead of staying at home.
To show that Confucius was born into a very poor family compared to his neighbors.

items.text: How does the author evaluate the long-term impact of Confucius’s life?
opts: By focusing on the fact that he failed to stay in government positions for a long time.
By describing the specific way he bound bamboo pages together.
By highlighting how his "beautiful thoughts" became an "indelible mark" on the national character of millions of people.
By proving that he was the only person in the state of Lu who knew how to write.

MOHAMMEDANISM, THE ISLAM FAITH
Have you ever wondered why our
Muslim brothers in Mindanao have a
different religion than ours? For a time,
Mohammedanism, or the Muslim
religion, threatened all Asia and even a
great part of Europe. Here's how
Mohammedanism came about.

The Mohammedan religion was founded by Mohammed and for a lime
was considered the most powerful religion in the world. There are still two
hundred thirty million believers of Mohammedan faith in Asia, Africa, and a
group in the Philippines, in Mindanao.

Mohammed, the founder of this religion, was born in Mecca in the years
570 A.D. His parents were poor and he received very little education. While
still a young boy he worked as a shepherd. At the age of 25, he married a rich
widow older than himself.

When he was about 40 years old, the Angel Gabriel appeared to him in
one of his prayers. The angel declared him as the prophet of God and told him
to preach the true religion.

Mohammed began to preach. His work was slow. He had only 40
followers after four years of preaching but he continued his work. He wrote
verses telling about the divinity of God and how mercy could be gained
through prayers, fasting, and alms- giving. These verses could be found at the
beginning of the Koran, the sacred book of the Mohammedans.

Mohammed was ever patient and never grew tired of preaching his
religion, He saw to it that his followers did not eat certain food. Later, he
prohibited them from drinking wine, gambling, and indulging is usury, His
followers lived by raiding caravans in the deserts and very often they were
Successful. Many people of Mecca joined the band of Mohammed.

Then came the years of misunderstanding and strife, War broke out
between the followers of Mohammed and the people of Mecca who did not
believe in him, Mohammed and his followers attacked Mecca and captured
the city in 630 A.D. The people rejoiced and honored him after his victory.

They considered him a prince and God's prophet on earth. He made many
conquests after this. His followers swept towards Asia and Africa, and for a
time, it was feared that Mohammedanism will succeed to engulf the whole
world.

However, Christianity triumphed in many places, and only some
countries remained Mohammedans — including the Muslims in Mindanao.

Read each question thoroughly. Choose the letter of the correct answer.

items.text: If you were an advisor to Mohammed during his first four years of preaching when he only had 40 followers, what creative strategy based on his character might you suggest to help his message reach more people?
opts: Suggest he give up preaching and return to being a shepherd.
Suggest he continue writing his verses to share with other caravan travelers, using his patience to slowly build trust.
Advise him to use his wife’s wealth to buy a larger army immediately.
Tell him to stop writing verses and only focus on raiding caravans for food.

items.text: Imagine a new city is being built today based strictly on the rules Mohammed established for his followers. Which of these businesses would likely be missing from that city?
opts: A public library filled with sacred books.
A school for teaching young children how to pray.
A casino that offers wine and gambling games.
A marketplace for trading silk and spices.

items.text: If the Angel Gabriel had not appeared to Mohammed when he was 40, how might his life have most likely continued based on his background before that event?
opts: He would have become a famous general in the Roman army.
He would have likely continued his life as a member of the merchant class or managed his family's interests in Mecca.
He would have moved to Mindanao to start a new colony.
He would have traveled to Europe to study at a university.

opts: By ignoring them and continuing on their journey to Mecca.
By challenging them to a race for the remaining supplies.
By practicing "alms-giving" and sharing their own food and water as an act of mercy.
By telling the person they should have prayed harder before they left.

items.text: If you were tasked with creating a modern "Peace Treaty" between the people of Mecca and Mohammed’s followers in 630 A.D., which of Mohammed's personal traits mentioned in the text would be most helpful in making the treaty last?
opts: His ability to lead successful raids on caravans.
His lack of formal education as a young boy.
His "ever patient" nature and his focus on mercy and divinity.
His victory in capturing the city by force.

acts.lead:
Read the selection below and answer the questions that follow.

THE IFUGAOS
The Ifugaos inhabiting the Mountain
Province of Northern Luzon are among
the most interesting people in the Far
East. They are direct descendants of the
earliest Malay invaders of the Philippines.
They have constructed one of the worlds
wonders.

Ifugao men wear clothes or G-strings;
the women wear short skirts reaching from waist to the knees, Men and
women alike wear ornaments of gold, beads, brass armlets and legless. They
build small but strong thatched houses.

The Ifugaos have many interesting customs. Once a girl reaches the
age of puberty, she is allowed to send the nights with other girls in the house
of some spinster or widow called” (ulog in Bontoc). Young men come to the
ayamang at night to express their love, The suitors are rejected or admitted
to the ayamang depending upon the reactions of the young maidens.

Trial marriage is practiced in the ayamang, A girl can live with the man
she prefers. When she is about to become a mother, arrangements are made
between their parents for their marriage.

Divorce may be had any time by either party on the Condition that the
dissatisfied party pays a fine to the family of the other. All the property of the
divorced spouses go to their children.

Ifugao customs and traditions abound in taboos, It is taboo for a
pregnant woman to wear ornaments forming a circle. It is believed that such
ornaments will make child delivery difficult,

People from one village cannot pass through another village during rice
harvest time. A stranger is not allowed to enter a village during its rest- day
celebration. Anyone is prohibited to enter an Ifugao house when the owner is
absent. A person doing so is considered a thief even if he has not taken
anything from the house.

The Ifugaos are lovers of law and order. Trial by ordeal by hot water or
the hot bolo test -----is practiced in trials for criminal offenses. The trial is a
punishment in itself. As a result, there are few crimes in Ifugao land.

Fines are assessed in accordance with the wealth of the offending party.
In this manner, a poor man Would not be required to pay a fine he cannot
afford.

We have always thought of the Ifugaos as Uncivilized. In the light of
their practices, could we still consider them as a society that achieved extraordinary
architectural and social milestones independently.

Read each question thoroughly. Choose the letter of the correct answer.

items.text: If you were a modern engineer visiting the Ifugao mountains, which aspect of their ancient "world wonder" would you study most to help build sustainable farms in other steep mountain regions?
opts: The specific types of G-strings and skirts worn by the workers.
Their system of stone-walled terraces and irrigation that prevents soil erosion on steep slopes.
The trial by ordeal methods used to settle disputes between villages.
The ornaments of gold and beads worn by the men and women.

items.text: Imagine you are a traveler approaching an Ifugao village during their "rest-day" celebration. Based on their taboos, what would be the most respectful and "creative" way to handle the situation?
opts: Enter the village anyway and offer gold beads as a peace offering.
Set up a camp outside the village limits and wait until the rest-day is over before attempting to enter.
Try to find a house where the owner is absent so you can rest quietly inside.
Walk through the village quickly while the people are busy with their harvest.

items.text: If an Ifugao leader wanted to modernize their "trial by ordeal" (hot water or hot bolo test) while still keeping their traditional focus on "law and order," what new method might they create?
opts: A race to the top of the highest mountain to see who is faster.
A system where the person who pays the most gold is found innocent.
A communal "Peace Council" where both parties must perform a community service task together to prove their sincerity.
Eliminating all trials and allowing people to take whatever they want from absent owners.

items.text: A pregnant Ifugao woman wants to follow the tradition of avoiding circular ornaments but still wants to look beautiful for a ceremony. Based on your creative understanding of the text, what could she wear instead?
opts: A heavy circular brass belt that covers her waist.
A necklace made of perfectly round gold beads.
Straight-lined brass armlets or rectangular woven patterns that do not form a complete circle.
A large circular hat made of thatched palm.

items.text: If the Ifugao "trial marriage" system in the ayamang was adapted into a modern school project about "responsibility," what would be the main lesson students would learn?
opts: That you should never listen to your parents' advice about marriage.
That big life decisions require a period of testing and mutual agreement between families before they become permanent.
That girls should live alone in the mountains until they become mothers.
That paying a fine is the best way to solve any problem in school.

Read the selection below and answer the questions that follow.

PLANT THIEVES
Most plants with green leaves
earn their own living. They do not
need help from other plants
inasmuch as they gather from the
soil and air the materials on which
they live. Their roots extend deep
into the soil seeking out water and
the substances the soil supplies.
Moreover, their leaves get carbon
dioxide from the air. With the help of
sunshine, they are able to manufacture their food. These plants do not destroy
other plants or animals or steal from them to obtain their food. These self-
supporting plants live and let other plants live.

But some plants are dependent on other plants. They also try to obtain
all the food they could by robbing their innocent victims. These plants have
no green-leaf substances and could not make for themselves. Such plants
are supplied entirely by their victims or hosts as they are usually called.

There are plant thieves that steal from their hosts as much as they can,
but because they have green leaves, they manufacture little food for
themselves, like all thieves, plant robbers have sneaking ways. They have
different ways of attacking their victims, The dodder is a plant that has a
tangle of yellow threads. In season, these yellow threads are vine- like sterna
twining about the branches of the host plant. The dodder has a bad
reputation as a plant thief in the plant world It has no roots nor leaves.
Instead, there are minute scales. With no roots nor leaves, the dodder grows
very well and bears flowers and seeds.

The secret of its food supply is the slender vines. These thin thread-like
stems are firmly fastened by rows of little suckers to the stems and branched
of the host plant. The suckers adhere to the host. The dodder sends minute
branches right through the bark of its victim into the part where the sap flows.
This way, it robs the host of its hard- earned riches supply itself with food for
its vigorous growth and for the formation of its cluster of flowers which it
shamelessly unfolds over the branches of its victim. The flowers, of course,
form abundant seeds to start a new crop of robbers for the next season.

items.text: If you were an artist creating a "villain" character for a comic book based on the dodder plant, which physical feature from the text would be the most accurate "weapon" for your character?
opts: Large green leaves that block the sunlight from others.
Deep, powerful roots that pull all the water out of the ground.
Slender, yellow thread-like arms with rows of "suckers" used to rob energy from victims.
Bright, colorful flowers that trick people into coming closer.

items.text: Imagine you have a garden where a "plant thief" has started to grow on your favorite rosebush. Based on how the dodder grows, what would be the most effective way to save your rosebush for the next season?
opts: Watering the dodder plant more so it doesn't have to steal from the rose.
Covering the rosebush with a blanket to hide it from the thief.
Carefully removing the dodder before it forms its "abundant seeds" to prevent a new crop of robbers from growing later.
Planting more green-leafed plants nearby to teach the dodder how to make its own food.

items.text: If the "self-supporting plants" and the "plant thieves" were human characters in a story about a community, which of these scenarios best represents the behavior of the "Plant Thieves"?
opts: A group of friends who share their snacks and help each other with homework.
A person who never brings their own tools to work and always secretly uses their neighbor's expensive equipment without asking.
A hard-working farmer who grows enough vegetables to feed the entire village.
A scientist who invents a new way to turn sunshine into electricity for everyone.

items.text: A scientist discovers a way to give "green-leaf substances" (chlorophyll) to a dodder plant through a special injection. Based on the logic of the text, how would the dodder's life most likely change?
opts: It might become less dependent on its host because it could finally manufacture some of its own food using sunshine.
It would grow even more suckers and kill the host plant twice as fast.
It would lose its yellow color and turn into a tree with deep roots.
It would immediately stop bearing flowers and seeds.

items.text: If you were writing a "Safety Guide for Plants," what would be the best advice for a "host" plant to avoid being attacked by a "thief" like the dodder?
opts: "Grow as many green leaves as possible to hide your stem."
"Deepen your roots so the thief cannot reach your water supply."
"Watch out for yellow, vine-like stems twining around your branches, as they want to send suckers through your bark."
"Try to grow only in the shade where the thief cannot find you."

POPE JOHN PAUL II
Pope John Paul II is Karol Wojtyla who
was born on May 18, 1920 to Karol and
Emilia Kaszrowska. His mother died when
he was nine years old. At the age of 21 his
father left him, too.

He graduated at the top of his class
when he was 18; began his college studies
at the City of Cracow; shifted to Theology in
secret during the German occupation, and
was ordained priest on November 1, 1946.
He was consecrated Bishop on September
28, 1958 and was made an Archbishop on
December 30, 1963. Four years later, on
May 29, 1967, he became a Cardinal. He
then became the Supreme Pontiff a position
naming him as the head of the Roman
Catholic religion.

Most notable about the Pope is his genuine and sterling love for
humanity, his great gearing for peace and love for all men, his keen
understanding of human frailties, and most of all, his concern for freedom
and human rights.

Pope John Paul II is completely averse to the luxury of pomp and
grandeur. He is at home in simple surroundings. Named the Head of the
church in Poland, he chose a room of Sparta surroundings. When he became
a Pope, he reprimanded the personnel staff who removed his belongings to a
more comfortable room during his absence. Briefly, he wanted a simple life,
sans the trimmings of a luxurious and kingly life.

On his first day as Supreme Pontiff, Pope John Paul II showed signs of
non- confinement within the walls of the Vatican. He disregarded the tradition
of seclusion. In less than 24 hours after assumption of office, he was up and
about and left the Vatican, much to the concern of the cautious officials, and
went to a Roman hospital to pay a visit to an old friend, Polish Bishop Andrzej
Maria Deskur. Once more he broke an age-long tradition of talking to a group
of hospital officials. As he is desirous to communicate with everyone, he

ignores protocol and goes as a politician would, shaking hands and kissing
babies.

When he came to the Philippines, he was not a stranger in our minds,
but a humble brother seeking to find old and new friends, a shepherd tending
a flock of sheep. He came as a leader to the only-Christian nation in the Far
East back then, the Philippines.

His message was one of brotherhood, peace, and loving sympathy for
the oppressed, the downtrodden, the. unjustly jailed, but most of all intended
to families who have a special place in his heart.

His death on April 2, 2005 was deeply mourned by all people, Catholic
and non-Catholic as well.

He left the legacy of "Service to others."
